meeting_header:
Date: 2027-06-30
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Tomas Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Alex Chen (CTO, Montara), Priya Rao (Infra Lead), Ethan Park (Head of ML), Sara Ibrahim (Security)
summary: Recurring renewal/expansion check-in. Customer evaluating increasing committed capacity across US-EAST and EU-West, plus pilot for private VPC deployment in APAC. Key concerns: data sovereignty, KMS integration, activation timeline, and unit cost at higher throughput. Agreement leaning toward 12-month committed uplift with staged regional activation and a private pilot in APAC. Next steps include updated quote, technical kickoff, and security artifacts exchange.
topics: Agenda: 1) Renewal terms and commitment sizing 2) Additional region onboarding (EU-West, APAC pilot) 3) Private deployment/VPC and KMS 4) Security/compliance questions 5) Next steps and timelines
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check of attendees, we have Alex, Priya, Ethan, Sara from Montara?
[00:06] Alex Chen: Yep, that’s right, thanks Jordan.
[00:08] Priya Rao: Hi, everyone.
[00:09] Ethan Park: Morning.
[00:10] Jordan Blake: Cool. Tomas and Maya on the Redwood side too. This is our regular renewal review — figure out sizing and the region playbook. We set 48 minutes, so we’ll try to keep it tight.
[00:20] Maya Singh: I can start with a quick run through of usage trends we saw last quarter and options for committed tiers — that’ll help ground the pricing conversation.
[00:27] Ethan Park: That would be great; our production traffic spiked last month, hence the capacity questions.
[00:31] Maya Singh: Right — looking at your token throughput, roughly 2.4x increase during peak windows, sustained over 8 weeks. Current Hosted plan can absorb bursts but the egress latency and cost scale nonlinearly at that level. Dedicated reserved capacity at the next tier reduces unit token cost and improves p95 latency by about 25% in our benchmarks, but it does require a 12-month commit for the economics to make sense.
[00:50] Alex Chen: We’re mostly worried about cost predictability and also data locality. Some of our EU customers require EU-only processing.
[00:56] Jordan Blake: Totally, that’s why we recommended pinning EU-West nodes and adding a geo-routing policy. We can route EU traffic to EU-only pools — can also add a fallback to US if desired.
[01:12] Priya Rao: For the APAC pilot, we’re exploring an on-prem-ish option — basically a private VPC deployment in an APAC region to satisfy latency and sovereignty. How mature is Redwood’s private offering there?
[01:24] Maya Singh: Our Private control plane is available in APAC via partners — there are a couple of options: a managed VPC with our control plane in a regional tenant, or a fully customer-managed on-prem installer. For the pilot in APAC, most customers do a managed VPC first — quicker activation around 2-3 weeks for staging. The fully air-gapped on-prem path takes longer (6-10 weeks) and requires deeper infra hooks.
[01:50] Sara Ibrahim: On the security side, we need KMS integration so keys never leave our cloud. We also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, RBAC mapped to our IdP, and confirmation of SOC2 scope.
[01:59] Maya Singh: On KMS — we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS and also HSM solutions. For the VPC case we can set up an envelope encryption path so your keys never leave your KMS. Audit logs can stream to your SIEM via syslog or S3 connectors. For SSO, we support SAML/SCIM for provisioning and RBAC mapping.
[02:23] Ethan Park: Quick question — does the KV cache work across regions or is it per-pool? We noticed performance differences in cross-region calls.
[02:31] Maya Singh: Good question. KV cache is per-pool — it’s colocated with the serving runtime. Cross-region cache misses do add latency; typical recommendation is prefix caching at the request router or local warm-up for cross-region fallbacks.
[02:45] Alex Chen: Hmm, so for multi-region we’ll need warm-up strategy or sticky routing for sessions.
[02:50] Jordan Blake: Exactly. We can do sticky session routing to keep a user's conversation pinned to a region until explicit failover. That reduces cross-region cache churn.
[02:59] Priya Rao: About the commitment sizing — Ethan, we’re looking at 3x our current sustained usage for safety. If we go to the next reserved tier, what discount does that unlock and what are the provisioning lead times?
[03:12] Maya Singh: For a 12-month commitment at the next tier, you get roughly 18-22% off hosted list for token pricing and a guaranteed capacity allocation. Provisioning for EU-West pools is typically 7-10 days; APAC partner-managed VPC usually 10-21 days due to region partner lead times. On-prem install as I said is longer.
[03:33] Alex Chen: That discount band helps. Any flexibility on month-to-month for burst? We need some seasonal burst headroom.
[03:39] Jordan Blake: We can include a burst buffer as part of the contract — an agreed burst pool with overage pricing. Typically customers do a buffer of 20-30% with a negotiated overage tier.
[03:52] Sara Ibrahim: From a procurement perspective we’ll want clear termination and data handling terms in the contract. Also need clarity on audit windows for SOC2.
[04:03] Tomas Alvarez: We’ll provide an addendum that clarifies data retention, egress, and audit windows. Also happy to share our SOC2 cert and scope doc.
[04:11] Priya Rao: For the private pilot, what does the provisioning window actually look like — step by step?
[04:16] Maya Singh: Step 1: technical kickoff and network prep (VPC CIDR, peering), Step 2: test staging deployment + smoke tests, Step 3: KMS/HSM integration and RBAC setup, Step 4: performance baseline and 72-hr soak, Step 5: cutover. Usually staging can be completed in 2-3 weeks if network prep is ready.
[04:34] Ethan Park: Can we run a throughput bench to validate p95 token latency? We want numbers for planning.
[04:39] Maya Singh: Yes — we can run a dedicated benchmark in your staging with your typical sequence-length distribution. It’s helpful if you share a representative prompt set. We can also test quantized variants and batching configs.
[04:52] Alex Chen: Are there any limits on model versions we can pin for production? We need predictable inference behavior.
[04:58] Maya Singh: You can pin model versions and rollout on a per-route basis. We also provide rollback and canary deploy policies in the console.
[05:06] Sara Ibrahim: One thing — our compliance team insists on keys rotated every 90 days and proof of separation of duties. Can Redwood support rotation automation?
[05:14] Maya Singh: Yes — KMS rotations are supported; for HSM-based it's customer managed but we integrate rotation hooks. Separation of duties is handled via RBAC and external IdP group mapping. We can include an ops playbook for the rotation flow.
[05:27] Priya Rao: About pricing tiers: if we commit for 12 months with multi-region (US-EAST + EU-WEST) and a small APAC private pilot, can you give a blended price?
[05:38] Jordan Blake: We’ll prepare an amended quote with blended pricing. Quick note — blended pricing depends on commit volume and whether the APAC pilot is managed VPC or on-prem. For managed VPC pilot we can include the APAC region as a staged activation at a small premium for the first 3 months, then fold into the committed base.
[05:58] Alex Chen: Timeline-wise we want EU activation before Q4 and APAC pilot by September. Is that feasible?
[06:04] Maya Singh: EU by late Sep is fine; we’d start provisioning mid-August to allow 4-6 week runway for testing and canary. APAC pilot by September is tight but possible if we do managed VPC and network prep is immediate.
[06:18] Ethan Park: For bench numbers — can you quantify the expected p95 improvement when moving from hosted to dedicated for our model family?
[06:25] Maya Singh: For models with ~2k token context and typical seq length distribution you sent, p95 improves roughly 20-30% and throughput doubles under continuous batching with dedicated pools. But I’ll run a representative benchmark with your prompt set to give exact numbers.
[06:40] Alex Chen: Any operational constraints — e.g., maintenance windows, planned upgrades, or forced rollbacks we should expect?
[06:46] Tomas Alvarez: We publish maintenance windows quarterly; critical patches can be fast-tracked but we notify customers. For Dedicated we have SLA-backed maintenance windows and a change advisory process.
[06:58] Priya Rao: On SLAs — can you confirm p95 latency SLA and uptime for dedicated pools?
[07:03] Tomas Alvarez: Our Dedicated SLA targets 99.9% uptime and latency SLOs depend on model and commit tier; we’ll include the SLO table in the quote.
[07:14] Sara Ibrahim: Legal will want indemnity language around data loss and clear responsibilities during peering or network faults.
[07:20] Jordan Blake: We’ll loop in legal and add contract language; Tomas can provide standard commodity clauses we use for dedicated and private deployments.
[07:30] Alex Chen: If we go with a 12-month commit, can we get a trial of private in APAC without the full long-term pricing? Like a 90-day pilot credit?
[07:39] Jordan Blake: We can propose a pilot credit in the amended quote as an incentive — usually we do partial credits tied to pilot milestones. I’ll include that option.
[07:50] Priya Rao: Network-wise we need to validate NAT and egress IP ranges — our legal team insists on known egress IPs to scope firewall rules.
[07:58] Maya Singh: We can provide fixed egress IP blocks for the VPC and document NAT behavior. For managed partner deployments, partner may allocate region-specific egress ranges.
[08:10] Ethan Park: On monitoring, we want token-level cost breakdown and per-route tracing into our APM. How deep does Redwood integrate?
[08:19] Tomas Alvarez: We expose per-token cost and latency via the console and APIs, and have tracing hooks that can forward spans to your APM. For private deployments we can also enable a higher data retention window for logs if needed.
[08:33] Priya Rao: Are there any blockers for us to get started with the kickoff next week if we sign?
[08:38] Jordan Blake: The only potential blocker is network prep from Montara; if you can provide CIDRs and firewall ownership, we can schedule staging immediately. Also need signed MSA with the commitment.
[08:49] Alex Chen: Okay, action items on our side: provide CIDR and compliance artifacts. Legal will review the amendment — we’ll aim to have that back in two weeks.
[08:58] Jordan Blake: Great. Quick recap — we’ll send an amended quote with blended pricing, pilot credit option, and a proposed activation timeline. Maya will drop the private deployment checklist and bench plan. Priya and team to share network details. Sara to share compliance artifact list.
[09:14] Sara Ibrahim: One last compliance question — do you support data residency enforcement at the route level? We want certain routes to never leave EU.
[09:22] Maya Singh: Yes, route-level residency policies are supported — you can pin routes to EU pools and block cross-region fallbacks for those routes. We’ll document how to set the policy in the console and the API.
[09:36] Alex Chen: Sounds good. Anything else from Redwood?
[09:40] Jordan Blake: Nothing else. Tomas — you want to add final notes?
[09:44] Tomas Alvarez: Just that we’ll include the SLA/maintenance table and standard SOC2 and pen-test artifacts. Expect the quote by 7/5.
[09:51] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. That timeline works.
[09:53] Jordan Blake: Thanks for the time — we’ll follow up in writing.
[09:58] [call ends]
